blocks.orig: November is the month for travelers who love to go a little off the beaten path. While many assume the short rains will spoil a safari, the reality is quite different — showers are usually brief, arriving in the late afternoon or evening, leaving most of the day bright and clear for game drives. The rains also transform the landscapes almost overnight, turning the dusty plains into lush, green backdrops that make wildlife sightings even more dramatic.

blocks.orig: Why November is a Great Time for Tanzania
blocks.html: Why November works so well for Tanzania

blocks.orig: Because November falls in Tanzania’s low season, you’ll find far fewer safari vehicles, more lodge availability, and excellent rates. It feels like the parks belong to you — just your vehicle, your guide, and the wildlife. Add to that the wildebeest herds moving back into the Serengeti from Kenya and the arrival of migratory birds, and you’ve got a safari experience that’s both unique and incredibly rewarding. November is for the traveler who wants space, value, and the thrill of seeing Tanzania in a different light.
blocks.html: Since November is part of Tanzania’s low season, you will come across far fewer safari vehicles, find more rooms available at the lodges and pay excellent rates. November suits the traveller who wants space, value and the chance to see Tanzania from a different angle.

blocks.orig: November brings Tanzania’s short rainy season, but don’t worry — it’s nothing like the heavy rains of April and May. Expect warm days averaging 25–30°C (77–86°F), with refreshing showers typically arriving in the late afternoon or evening. Most of the day remains clear and perfect for game drives.
